configKeys.effect: How often every tracked logistics link is re-stamped in Create's LINKS cache. That cache expires 20 ticks - one second - after a link last refreshed it, and only the link's own lazyTick() does that, which needs a TICKING chunk. Must stay below 20; 5 leaves a margin of four.
How long factory panels are held after their chunk loads, before the condition below takes over. Covers the case where the chunks really did unload and the links have to register from scratch.

Keep holding a gauge past grace_ticks while its network summary has no contributing links at all (InventorySummary.contributingLinks == 0). A fixed wait is always a guess; this is the fact the guess stood for. Bounded by max_hold_ticks.

Ceiling on how long one gauge may be held, counted from its chunk load. Only reached when a network genuinely has no contributing links - measured on five gauges whose network has none at all. They are then released and Create decides for itself again.
Whether the chunk-load hold runs at all. The keepalive above is unaffected by this key.

notes:
THE ACTUAL BUG, AND TWO WRONG FIXES BEFORE IT. A Factory Gauge orders when its item is below target and Create's guard waitingForNetwork is false. Stock comes from LogisticsManager.getSummaryOfNetwork(), built from LogisticallyLinkedBehaviour.getAllPresent(), i.e. the static LINKS cache - a TickBasedCache(20, true), so an entry dies ONE SECOND after its last refresh. The only thing that refreshes it is the link's own lazyTick(), which requires the link's chunk to be TICKING. The guard meanwhile comes from totalLinks.size() - loadedLinks.size(), which was 0 in every single sample taken on this network, healthy or not - so it can never fire here. getUnloadedLinkCount() also returns 0 when the network object is absent entirely, a second silent way for the guard to vanish.

THE TRIGGER (reproduced by the server owner, 2026-09-23): step into the chunk diagonally NE of the stock link's chunk, step back, then reconnect. Log: left at 20:57:39.697, joined at 20:57:41.132 - a gap of 1.4 seconds. Chunks do NOT unload that fast, so NO ChunkEvent.Load fires at all; the module logged nothing for the whole run. But a disconnecting player takes their chunk tickets with them, so the chunks stop TICKING immediately while staying loaded. 1.4 s > 1.0 s, so the LINKS entries expire, the summary goes empty, and because nothing unloaded, loadedLinks still lists every link and the guard stays false. The gauge ticks on reconnect, reads 0 from a full vault, and orders. Confirmed by stock: fluid tank 81->82, oak chest 74->75, chain drive 108->109 across that single run. The absence can be ANY length over one second - it only has to be shorter than the chunk-unload delay.

TWO FIXES THAT MISSED, AND WHY THEY ARE KEPT. (1) A fixed 60-tick hold after chunk load: held on one rejoin, was too short on the next. (2) The same hold extended while contributingLinks == 0: better, but still tied to ChunkEvent.Load - and the reproducible case has no chunk load whatsoever. Both remain in the module because they cover the OTHER regime, where the chunks really did unload and the links must register from scratch; 27 releases were logged during the successful verification run. The fix that actually closes the reproducible case is keepLinksAlive(), which re-stamps every tracked link from the module's own ServerTickEvent - that keeps running no matter which chunks tick, so the cache cannot run dry for any length of absence.

VERIFIED 2026-09-23 over FIVE consecutive rejoins using the owner's exact reproduction: fluid tank 82, oak chest 75, barrel 104, chain drive 109 - unchanged to the item, LastPromised 0 on every panel, zero errors, 20.000 TPS. One passing run is NOT evidence for a timing-dependent fix; that lesson cost three premature all-clears in one evening.

WHY resetTimer() AND NOT A FIELD: tickRequests() returns while timer > 0, before it reads any stock level, and resetTimer() is public. Setting waitingForNetwork directly would not work - tickStorageMonitor() recomputes it earlier in the same tick.

Upstream: the guard half is reported as Create issue #10774. The cache-expiry half found here is not yet reported.
oneLiner: Factory Gauges stop ordering a fresh batch of something the vault is already full of after you rejoin, because the logistics links are kept reporting their contents even while nobody is nearby to make their chunks tick.

requiredMods.evidence: CreateStockLinkKeepaliveModule.java - shouldInitialize() returns isCreateLoaded(), i.e. ModList.get().isLoaded("create"). Without Create, AbstractModule.initialize() skips onInitialize() entirely, so no event handler is ever registered and the module is inert. No Create type is referenced at compile time anywhere in this module: block detection goes through BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK.getKey(state.getBlock()) compared against a ResourceLocation, and every block-entity access goes through the reflection-only bridge class. That is deliberate - Create's SmartBlockEntity hierarchy drags in Ponder, which is not safe to reference from a dedicated-server build (see the project's create-integration note). The bridge resolves all its handles in a static initializer that catches Throwable; if any lookup fails, isAvailable() returns false and the module stays inert instead of throwing. Create is therefore REQUIRED for this module to do anything.

shortDescription: Stops Create Factory Gauges from re-ordering stock they already have, right after a chunk load.
